reported_symptom: User reports air mouse no longer moves
confirmed_defect: Output ownership and logical screen pose transitions discard otherwise valid native sensor calibration samples

reproduction.implementation_under_test: actual AUTO touch and IMU drivers plus actual motion core; fake hardware and scheduler
reproduction.stimulus: 10 repetitions of 120 ms ambiguous touch followed by 140 ms genuine no-touch while gyro remains stationary
reproduction.before_fix: ASAN/UBSAN host regression fails: no valid bias after 2600 ms
reproduction.after_fix: Host regression passes: calibration completes, uncertain touch emits no HID, resumed output starts without accumulated displacement
additional_checks: Logical pose changes every 120 ms do not reset calibration in native sensor axes
Accelerometer or gyro I2C failure every 200 ms still prevents calibration
After sensor errors stop, 2400 ms of continuous stable data permits automatic calibration
Gyro is powered up once throughout output ownership changes

sleep_wake_defect.confirmed_defect: Sleep blocks output, clears integration every poll and restores AUTO RAW; wake was reachable only through already-authorized pointer displacement
sleep_wake_defect.before_fix: Actual driver host test fails: after 10 seconds asleep, 200 ms corrected gyro movement never wakes the display
sleep_wake_defect.after_fix: The same test passes: sustained fresh calibrated gyro movement wakes without any pointer report, AUTO independently re-arms and confirms idle before movement resumes
sleep_wake_defect.wake_policy: Fresh native zero-contact report at most 100 ms old, no capture or pending button, connected endpoint, status page, fresh gravity and calibrated gyro; the SAME three-axis projected yaw or pitch rate used by the pointer must exceed the existing 80-count deadband for 60 ms with sample gaps at most 40 ms
guards_tested: Contact, malformed/failed/stale native reports and pending buttons block gyro wake
No HID endpoint or non-status page blocks gyro wake
One 20 ms motion sample followed by rest cannot wake
First wake frame has no HID and no integration backlog
Three enable/disable cycles with endpoint transitions retain stationary calibration
sleep_wake_defect.scope: Host reproduction with fake hardware, not evidence of successful physical air mouse behavior

follow_up_passive_observation.note: Buffered initialization lines only; neither runtime enable state nor successful physical motion was established. No sampling or flash command was sent.

user_confirmed_grips: flat screen up with screen top pointing forward
upright screen facing user with rear pointing forward
three_axis_projection.prior_mapping_defect: Only gx and gy were used; flat screen-up yaw can be almost entirely gz and was ignored
three_axis_projection.model: UP is trusted normalized support acceleration; horizontalRight is normalized(screenRight - UP * dot(screenRight,UP)); logical rates x=-dot(gyroMinusBias,UP), y=-dot(gyroMinusBias,horizontalRight)
three_axis_projection.trajectory_regression: 20 ms physical gravity/gyro pairs at 15.75 deg/s pitch, 0 to almost 90 degrees and reverse, with and without simultaneous world yaw, in all four screen orientations
three_axis_projection.mounting_evidence: Existing empirically confirmed planar gravity/display orientation; front normal -Z is the right-handed inference from native +X down and +Y left, not a new physical Z-axis measurement
three_axis_projection.reference_scope: Reference uses fixed -gz/gy on its mounting; its hard-coded mapping is NOT copied as a universal orientation model

limitation: Host reproduction and analytic motion vectors establish software behavior only. Without enabled-state physical motion logs, neither the sole cause of the user's observed stop nor the real grip direction/feel is established. No physical device flash or HID injection was performed during this investigation.
